name: Mexican Brothy Beans and Pork With Salsa Macha and Cilantro Pesto

cookwares.name: stock pot or large Dutch oven

ingredients.name: dried large butter beans, such as royal corona
kosher salt, plus more to taste
dried chiles árbol chiles, stem removed
neutral oil, such as canola or vegetable oil

instructions.primary_message: In a large pot, combine pork, onion, carrot, garlic, bay leaves, and 2 teaspoons kosher salt. Cover with 3000 ml water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low and cook, covered, at a gentle simmer until the pork begins to become tender and a knife inserted meats no resistance, about 2 hours. Add beans and continue to cook until pork can be easily pierced with a fork and beans are tender, 1 ½ to 2 hours longer.

For the Salsa Macha: Meanwhile, in a food processor, add árbol chiles and process until coarse flakes form. Set aside. In a small pot, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add almonds and fry, stirring frequently, until fragrant and golden, about 2 minutes. Add ground árbol chile flakes, cumin, and oregano. Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds more. Set aside.

For the Salsa Verde Pesto: To the now-empty food processor, add cilantro, serranos, and garlic, and process, scraping down sides halfway through with a flexible spatula, until ingredients are finely minced, about 1 minute. With the machine running, drizzle in olive oil until smooth. Add Parmesan and pulse to combine. Season with salt to taste. Set aside.

When beans and pork are ready to serve, use a large slotted spoon to remove onion, carrot, garlic, and bay leaves (discard or compost). Remove pork and transfer to a cutting board. Using 2 forks, shred pork into bite-size pieces, then return to pot. Gently stir to incorporate without rupturing beans. Season to taste with salt.
Serve brothy pork and beans with warm tortillas and lime wedges. Top with generous portions of salsa macha and salsa verde pesto.

schema_metadata.keywords: Mexican Brothy Beans, Mexican Brothy Beans and Pork With Salsa Macha and Cilantro Pesto, Pork and Beans Recipe

description: This recipe for brothy Mexican beans calls for simmering pork shoulder and butter beans until tender, then finishing them with a crunchy almond salsa macha and a bright cilantro-serrano pesto for a filling and impressive meal.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Warm tortillas and lime wedges for serving

Make-ahead and storage: The pork and beans can be stored in their cooking liquid in an airtight container for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
The salsa verde pesto and salsa macha can be refrigerated separately in airtight containers for up to 7 days.
author: Octavio Peña
